# route_package_window with its parameter renamed `id`, which is what the GET
# handler already called the session id. `sess`, `ok` and `s` are three more of
# the same: an href may claim any of them, and only `w` and `r` had been
# prefixed out of the way.
#
# `{s}` was the worst of them, because it rewrote a signature rather than a
# statement -- `func renderHandlePage(s *handlePageState, s string) string`.
#
# The handler's own bindings are allocated around the program's name now, so
# the parameter keeps `id` and the session id becomes `id2`.
#
# This has to compile, not parse: a redeclaration is valid Go syntax, so
# `format.Source` accepted it and `sngl generate` exited 0.

sngl generate --lang go --platform html -o out app.sngl

exec go build ./...

grep 'id := __r.PathValue\("id"\)' out/server.go
grep 'id2, ok := snglSessionID' out/server.go
grep 'renderHandlePage\(s, id\)' out/server.go

-- go.mod --
module paramname

go 1.24

-- srv/srv.go --
package srv

func Bump(n int) int { return n + 1 }

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import "go:paramname/srv"
import "sngl:platform/html"

var hits = 0

window #page(title="t", href="/p/{id}") {
    html.button(innerText="go", @click { hits = srv.Bump(hits) })
    html.span(innerText="{id}{hits}")
}
